title: Understanding ASP File Execution
subtopics: Why server-side code is not sent as executable VBScript to the client
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of understanding asp file execution in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: How IIS recognizes .asp files and Server-side execution versus browser-side execution.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study understanding asp file execution as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 13 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding ASP File Execution matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This topic connects HTTP and IIS configuration to the actual Classic ASP request path. The `.asp` extension alone does not guarantee execution: the relevant IIS feature, application mapping, site binding, physical path, permissions, and provider/runtime dependencies all matter. Diagnose one layer at a time and use a test site rather than changing production defaults blindly.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: How IIS recognizes .asp files; Server-side execution versus browser-side execution; Processing ASP script blocks; Returning HTML to the browser; Why server-side code is not sent as executable VBScript to the client. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Understanding ASP File Execution
content_blocks.code:
<%
Dim message
message = "Server-side only"
Response.Write Server.HTMLEncode(message)
%>
content_blocks.expected_output: The browser receives the rendered text `Server-side only`, not the VBScript statements.
content_blocks.run_instructions: View the page source returned by IIS, not the file through the filesystem, to distinguish server code from generated HTML. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. This block is therefore marked for static inspection unless you run it in the clearly identified local tool.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original sample and test data. Change one condition, input, provider setting, or runtime option at a time, then compare observed behavior with the expected result.
content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Run the example only on a local or test IIS site with the Classic ASP feature enabled. Record the OS, IIS version, site binding, physical directory, and the exact URL used. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of understanding asp file execution. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
